claims.statement: Marina Barrage combines water storage, flood alleviation and public recreation.
claims.limitations: Physical representation will be schematic; this is not a surveyed model.

claims.statement: PUB describes a 350 m wide Marina Channel spanned by the barrage.
claims.limitations: Physical representation will be schematic; this is not a surveyed model.

claims.statement: There are nine steel crest gates; PUB describes each as 30 m long and 5 m tall.

evidence.locator: PDF page 1, The Barrage / Marina Bridge

claims.limitations: Rounded public dimensions; do not infer a 270 m total structure length or fabricate fabrication tolerances.

claims.statement: Seven vertical-shaft axial-flow drainage pumps are rated at 40 cubic metres per second each; PUB gives 280 combined with all seven operating.
claims.limitations: Axial-flow type is single-source PUB; installed capacity is not guaranteed discharge at arbitrary head or a claim all pumps run continuously.

claims.statement: PUB lists a 1600 kW electric motor for each drainage pump.
claims.limitations: Historical published specification, not a live equipment audit; no full-load energy calculator inferred.

claims.statement: In heavy rain at low tide, gates release excess reservoir water to sea; PUB describes the gates as lowering.

evidence.locator: PDF page 1, The Barrage / Marina Bridge

claims.limitations: Both sources are PUB, not independent corroboration. Avoid reversed gate motion.

claims.statement: Pumps discharge excess stormwater when high tide prevents the low-tide gravity-release mode.
claims.limitations: Teaching states are simplified; not actual dispatch instructions.

claims.statement: Gate operation depends on weather, reservoir level and tide, with no predetermined opening schedule.
claims.limitations: No operator thresholds, telemetry, pump dispatch algorithm or live control simulation available.

claims.statement: The Marina catchment is about 10,000 hectares; PUB identifies upstream rivers and canals feeding it.
claims.limitations: Catchment land area, not reservoir water surface. Both sources same agency; no exact GIS boundary licensed.

claims.statement: Collected stormwater requires treatment for drinking; it is separate from the used-water sewer system.

evidence.locator: Rainwater collection and separate used-water system

claims.limitations: Drainage pumps shown discharge to sea; no fictional pipe into DTSS or direct drinking-water outlet.

claims.statement: Construction began in 2005; the Barrage opened on 31 October 2008.
claims.limitations: Physical representation will be schematic; this is not a surveyed model.

claims.statement: Natural desalting began in April 2009; Marina Reservoir was commissioned as freshwater on 20 November 2010.
claims.limitations: 2010 date corroborated; April 2009 single-source PUB. Desalting by rain replacement differs from a desalination plant.

claims.statement: The late-1980s vision faced water-quality and treatment constraints; river cleanup and improved membrane treatment helped make urban-catchment water feasible.
claims.limitations: Retrospective government history, not a contemporary alternatives appraisal or proof of a specific gate procurement decision.

claims.statement: The landscaped green roof provides recreation and building insulation.
claims.limitations: No claim solar panels run the drainage pumps; omit dated largest-solar-park superlative.

claims.statement: Tsurumi reports supplying construction dewatering and slurry pumps from 2005.

evidence.locator: Case study introduction and equipment table

claims.limitations: Supplier account only; these are temporary construction pumps, not the seven permanent drainage pumps.

claims.statement: The project-authored paper describes a sand-filled double-sheet-pile marine cofferdam.

evidence.locator: Indexed abstract, temporary works paragraph; full primary-host text inaccessible

claims.limitations: Concept only. No verified detailed layout, exact depths, two-phase gate allocation, tie-rod sizes or excavation sequence approved for factual reconstruction.

claims.statement: PUB announced a Marina Barrage retrofit for future sea-level rise in 2025.

evidence.locator: Greater Southern Waterfront / Marina Barrage retrofit

claims.limitations: Documented proposal, not completed works or a confirmed 2050 delivery date.

claims.statement: PUB identifies possible beams and seals between crest gates and bridge as a future adaptation.

evidence.locator: Upgrading Marina Barrage for future sea levels

claims.limitations: Conditional concept; any ghosted geometry labelled envisioned, not final design.

claims.statement: Rain, relative water levels and animated arrows will illustrate drainage choices qualitatively.
claims.limitations: No flood depths, CFD, salinity kinetics, exact operating thresholds or geographic inundation prediction.

claims.statement: 1958, 1965 and 2000 precede the documented 2005 construction start.
claims.limitations: Temporal inference only. Current coastline remains explicitly modern context; no invented historic shoreline.
